messages.author: 929e733ff7821ad3
messages.subject: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(), status 253
parts:
Dear all,

I have a very large data set of 181362 rows and I am running R-inla with a list of fixed effects, as shown below

formula  <- presence ~ depth + slope + aspect + dist2coast + gannet_dist + day_of_season + SOURCE_DB + sediment + offset(logopp)

M1 <- inla(presence ~ 1,
           family            = "binomial",
           data              = dat,
           control.compute   = list(dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE),
           control.predictor = list(
             compute = TRUE,
             quantiles = c(0.025, 0.975)
           ), verbose=TRUE, num.threads=1, control.inla = list(strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb")
           )

All my covariates are standadized to avoid numeric problems. The output gives error message as:  Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(), ... status 253

If I run under the simplest formula: presence ~ 1, it worked.

1) I have tried both options: num.threads=1 and control.inla = list(strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb") . However, it still gives the same error message.

2) Since my data contains 27 years of data, I tried to reduce the size of my data to reduce memory usage. However, the error message disappears only if I keep the last 4 years data (=37381 rows). This is not acceptable for me.

3) The full expected model that I would like to apply will contain also a year smoother as rw1 model and a spatial spde model. When I run the full model, it seems that it's working without a fast pompt of the error message. But I dont know how long will it last and whether it will show the same error message later, that's why I tried the simplier model above and encountered the error message.

My questions are:

1. is it possible that the full model can run without error while the simplier model gives crash error message? if so, then I can directly run my full model, just need to wait for a long time

2. any solutions to solve the crash, without compromising the size of my data or model complexity

3. if R-inla can not technically help. Is there any practical suggestions? for instance, reduce the model complexity...

Thanks very much

Chun Chen

messages.author: 68c425efdf6bd7f6
messages.subject: Re: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(), status 253
parts:
Hi Chun,

have you tried to take a sample of the data? This would help to determine whether it is just the data size (and your hardware - lack of memory?) or if the problem lies somewhere else. My suggestion is to run the model with e.g. a 10% subset of the data; you could group your sample by year:

 sample <- stratified(data, group = year, size = 0.1, keep.rownames = TRUE)

Did you check for data incosistencies including NA values? Also, you could run in verbose = TRUE to check where exactly the model crashes. Similarly, you might run the taskmanager to check if it crashes just because the memory is full.

I ran into a comparable issue with a large dataset and setting control.inla(......, reordering = "amdc") solved the issue.

messages.subject: Re: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(), status 253
parts:
Thanks Boris and Havard for the suggestions on diagnostics. It turned out my computer memory is too low, only 8GB. I tried my code on a Linux  mac with 16GB and it worked. 

Thanks

Chun
